note if they are clear despite the presence of cardiac silhouette enlargement.", "Correlate the anatomical finding (widened left superior mediastinum) with the physiological symptom (hypoxaemia) by considering a Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava (PLSVC) draining into the left atrium.", "Distinguish this from left heart failure (which would typically show pulmonary venous congestion) or compressive masses (which would not inherently cause shunting/hypoxaemia without airway compromise)."]}, {"category": "reasoning", "trigger": "When determining the initial management for a patient with a large pleural effusion identified on chest imaging.", "steps": ["Confirm the presence of a large pleural effusion by identifying homogeneous opacity in the hemithorax that obscures the hemidiaphragm and costophrenic angle, potentially with a meniscus sign or mediastinal shift to the contralateral side.", "Distinguish thoracentesis as the primary initial intervention over observation (insufficient for large/symptomatic cases), antibiotics (only if infection is confirmed and not the sole mechanical fix), or surgery (reserved for complex/loculated cases) based on the need for immediate symptomatic relief via drainage and fluid acquisition for diagnostic analysis."]}]
